response.title: what can a 350 watt power station run
response.answer:

markup:
A **350-watt portable power station** can run many small electronics, including laptops, TVs, fans, lights, Wi-Fi routers, and some mini fridges. However, it generally cannot run high-power appliances like microwaves, electric kettles, or space heaters.

## What can a 350W power station run?

| Device | Typical power consumption | Can it run? |
|---|---:|---|
| Smartphone charger | 5–20W | <icon name="check-circle" color="success" inline/> Yes |
| Wi-Fi router | 5–20W | <icon name="check-circle" color="success" inline/> Yes |
| LED light | 5–15W | <icon name="check-circle" color="success" inline/> Yes |
| Laptop | 30–100W | <icon name="check-circle" color="success" inline/> Yes |
| Electric fan | 20–75W | <icon name="check-circle" color="success" inline/> Yes |
| 32–55" LED TV | 40–150W | <icon name="check-circle" color="success" inline/> Yes |
| CPAP machine | 30–100W | <icon name="check-circle" color="success" inline/> Usually |
| Mini fridge | 50–100W | <icon name="alert-circle" color="warning" inline/> Depends on startup surge |
| Desktop computer | 150–500W | <icon name="alert-circle" color="warning" inline/> Depends |
| Blender | 300–1,000W | <icon name="x-circle" color="danger" inline/> Usually no |
| Coffee maker | 600–1,500W | <icon name="x-circle" color="danger" inline/> No |
| Microwave | 800–1,500W | <icon name="x-circle" color="danger" inline/> No |
| Electric kettle | 1,000–1,500W | <icon name="x-circle" color="danger" inline/> No |
| Space heater | 750–1,500W | <icon name="x-circle" color="danger" inline/> No |

You can also run multiple devices simultaneously, as long as their **combined power consumption stays below 350W**.

## How long will it run?

This depends on the battery capacity, measured in watt-hours (Wh), not just the 350W output rating.

For example, assuming your power station has a **300Wh battery**, here's an interactive runtime calculator.

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(60)}
{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("300")}
{@body const hours = Number(capacity)*0.85/watts}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <text weight="medium">Estimated battery runtime</text>
  <row justify="between" align="center">
    <box gap={1}>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Runtime</text>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{Math.floor(hours)}h {Math.round((hours%1)*60)}m</title>
    </box>
    <box gap={1} align="end">
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Power draw</text>
      <title size="lg" tabularNums>{watts}W</title>
    </box>
  </row>
  <text color="secondary" size="xs">Battery capacity</text>
  <radio-group value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity} direction="row">
    <radio value="200">200Wh</radio>
    <radio value="300">300Wh</radio>
    <radio value="500">500Wh</radio>
  </radio-group>
  <row justify="between" align="center">
    <label>Device power consumption</label>
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{watts}W</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={10} max={350} step={10} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  <row justify="between">
    <text color="tertiary" size="xs">10W</text>
    <text color="tertiary" size="xs">350W</text>
  </row>
  <caption>Estimates assume 85% usable energy after conversion losses. Actual runtime varies by device and power station.</caption>
</box>

**Important:** A 350W power station has two separate specifications:

- **350W output:** The maximum continuous power it can supply.
- **Battery capacity (Wh):** How long it can power your devices.

Some appliances also require a brief startup surge above their normal running wattage.

**What brand and model is your 350W power station?** I can tell you exactly what appliances it can handle and estimate how long each will run.
